# The Veil of the Heavens

## Scripture

*"He sits enthroned above the circle of the earth, and its people are like grasshoppers. He stretches out the heavens like a canopy, and spreads them out like a tent to live in."* — Isaiah 40:22

## Reflection

On clear autumn evenings, if you travel far from city lights, you can see the Andromeda Galaxy—a faint smudge of light against the darkness. What appears as a wisp of cloud is actually 2.5 million light-years away, a spiral of a trillion stars. Our ancestors called it "the little cloud," never knowing they were glimpsing a neighbor galaxy.

Isaiah tells us God stretches out the heavens like a tent—a dwelling place. The same hands that spread galaxies across the void also hold our small lives with care. The God who measures the universe with the span of His hand (Isaiah 40:12) still counts the hairs on our heads.

This is the mystery of autumn's fading light: as the world grows quieter and darker, the heavens open wider. The veil between earth and infinity grows thin. We see farther into the cosmos, and we remember how far God's love reaches—past every star, every galaxy, every cloud of ancient light, all the way to us.

When the night feels vast and you feel small, remember: you are not lost in the expanse. You are held by the One who made it all and calls each star by name.

## Prayer

Lord of the expanding heavens, thank You for stretching out the sky like a tent and still making room for us. When we feel small beneath the autumn stars, remind us that Your love reaches farther than the farthest galaxy. Help us rest in Your vast care tonight. Amen.
